title: Check the complete P104 price with exact root certificates
body:
The complete PR6453 price verifier now accepts a directly checked raw-root certificate instead of repeating binary search. The replacement preserves both independent arithmetic engines, strict endpoint signs, monotonicity, the complete signed invoice, strictification, compiler and all 54 strict/four functional outer predicates. The entire encoded price receipt equals the retained source receipt.

For a changed invoice, an exact rational interval-Newton producer reaches the same adjacent `10^-26` bracket in four contractions. A global second-derivative bound lets each step reuse the moment's exact powers for its derivative. Invalid grid, adjacency, endpoint sign and derivative/image cases reject. This is the existing source crossing; it supplies no new kappa or extra-digit claim.

Validation: registered normal and optimized CPython 3.12 replay; four exact contractions and ten rejection controls; complete baseline/candidate price equality; committed bytes/modes; official 26-file export and input coverage. Read-only Git-free empty-PATH replays also pass with identical scientific receipts and source-corruption rejection. The checkout is shallow, so full-history checking is unrun; every live pin points to the retained-input ancestor on this branch. Exact nested source archive paths and retained byte hashes are recorded.

Three alternating fresh-process pairs through the complete price module all return the same receipt. Medians are 39.81 seconds baseline and 29.62 seconds candidate, but the ranges overlap substantially (24.93–44.14 versus 26.36–41.09 seconds). **No reliable runtime speedup is established.** The exact work reduction is zero root-search iterations during certificate verification. All measurements and source/input hashes are retained.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-interval-root-replay`.

Scope: native and caller receipts are authenticated inputs, not newly regenerated proofs. No full native replay, physical backend, rounded multiplier, selected-frontier change or independent scientific acceptance is claimed. All five framework assumptions remain. The next arithmetic question is whether large rational denominators in the second engine can be reduced while preserving rigorous enclosures and the complete price receipt.

Base and submission refresh: canonical main `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, revision 8, selected PR6030. Complete overlap coverage: 430 open PRs and 6,399 discussion records, plus a final live refresh. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5600#discussioncomment-19363340); the canonical thread records expansion from the raw-root kernel to complete price verification. PR6478 concerns Newton falling-factor precision and has a different source and quantity.

Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. Classical interval Newton is not claimed as new. zxv, Cao Yifan, Jacob Alan Sussman and the retained interval/compiler/outer authors retain credit. Erwan L., Rohan Arun, DreamingOfClouds, Cinna Davis, David Arias, Gareth Davidson and the P104/caller lineage retain their construction credit. Changes are isolated in `research/p104-interval-root-replay/`.
